newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean politicians go on trial for bribery.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean politicians go on trial for bribery.

text.p: Another close political associate of South Korean President Kim Young-sam and seven serving or former lawmakers went on trial on Monday on charges of taking bribes from the founder of the controversial Hanbo group.
Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, who was jailed last month for 15 years in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal, was again charged with bribing the politicians.
The scandal has already landed three close associates of the president -- one a former cabinet minister -- in jail along with bankers and businessmen.
Among the eight on trial on Monday were Moon Jung-soo, mayor of South Korea's second largest city, Pusan, and two serving lawmakers.

Moon, a member of Kim's inner circle that played a leading role in his 1992 election victory, pleaded not guilty to charges that he had received kickbacks of 200 million won ($224,000) before being elected as Pusan mayor in 1995.
State prosecutors accused the eight of accepting money from the founder of Hanbo, whose steel-making flagship collapsed in January under five trillion won of debts, revealing a web of corruption.
Moon and one other defendant said they had not received a cent from Hanbo, court officials said.
The other six admitted receiving money from Hanbo but denied it was bribery, the officials said.
A public furore over the Hanbo scandal led to the probe into President Kim's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, dealing a dire blow to Kim's presidency.
The prosecution has cleared Kim Hyun-chul of any involvement in the loans-for-kickbacks scandal, but arrested him on charges of bribery in unrelated cases and on tax evasion.
Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo's Chung helped bankroll the president's 1992 election victory and that Kim Hyun-chul laundered huge sums of leftover funds through business cronies.
Kim Young-sam last month apologised for spending a large sum on his election campaign but refused to yield to opposition demands that he reveal details of the financing.
The trial was adjourned until June 30.
